channel.title: Blocktape
channel.description: Blocktape reports crypto news: exchange and market moves, protocol upgrades, token launches, security incidents, regulation and enforcement across chains.

item.title: Ethereum Foundation launches zkAPI for private AI payments
item.description: Ethereum Foundation and Open Anonymity launched zkAPI on mainnet, using zero-knowledge proofs to separate AI API payments from user identities for metered services.

item.title: Chainflip Bitcoin-to-Solana Swaps Usually Take About 30 Minutes
item.description: A Bitcoin-to-Solana swap on Chainflip usually waits about 30 minutes for Bitcoin confirmations; Boost may shorten the wait, while network delays can extend it.

item.title: Check BSC Token Charts Before You Swap
item.description: A BSC token chart shows past trades in a selected pool, while your swap quote estimates a new trade; check the contract, liquidity and price impact before signing.

item.title: How to Deposit USDT Into a TRON Lending Market
item.description: A TRON USDT deposit needs a compatible wallet, TRC-20 USDT, transaction resources and a token approval; the market then issues a receipt and applies variable interest.

item.title: TRON USDT approvals: set a limit and verify the spender
item.description: A TRC-20 approval lets a named contract spend your USDT up to a limit. Check the token, spender and amount before signing, then review or revoke the allowance.

item.title: Batch USDT transfers need recipient-by-recipient Energy estimates
item.description: Size a TRON USDT batch by estimating each recipient’s transfer cost, adding the results and checking available Energy before broadcasting transactions.

item.title: How XMR Bridge Reserves Handle Overlapping Swaps
item.description: XMR bridge reserves let swaps overlap by tracking committed funds separately from spendable inventory, then releasing each allocation after settlement or refund.

item.title: How to Choose a USDT Network for an XMR Bridge
item.description: Choose the USDT network your receiving wallet explicitly supports, then compare net payout, transfer costs and settlement steps before sending XMR.

item.title: How Blackhole voters can swap weekly rewards into AVAX
item.description: Blackhole voters can claim weekly fees and bribes, then swap supported Avalanche assets into AVAX on C-Chain after checking the quote, token address and gas.

item.title: Read Active Price Ranges Before You Swap
item.description: A pool’s price range shows where liquidity can absorb a trade; compare active depth, quoted price impact and fees before choosing a swap route for your trade.

item.title: Token names are labels; contract addresses establish identity
item.description: A token’s name and symbol are labels, not proof of origin. Check its network, address and verified code against issuer details before trading or approving.

item.title: Estimate Pool Loss Before You Add Liquidity
item.description: Estimate a liquidity pool’s loss by comparing its post-price token value with holding the same tokens, then subtract likely fees and incentives before depositing.

item.title: Why a Cross-Chain Transfer Can Stay Pending
item.description: A pending cross-chain transfer can mean the source transaction is confirmed while destination delivery or settlement is still underway; check both chains before retrying.

item.title: Choose a wallet that can deliver native cross-chain payouts
item.description: A suitable wallet must control payout keys, accept the destination chain’s native asset, and show total fees and settlement status clearly before each transfer.

item.title: Broker commission: check the fee before retrying a swap
item.description: A broker commission is one part of a swap’s cost; check how it is charged, what changed since the failed quote and whether retrying uses a fresh route.

item.title: Pool Execution vs CEX Order Books: How Crypto Trades Fill
item.description: Pool execution prices swaps against shared liquidity, while CEX order books match bids and asks; learn how routing, depth, fees and slippage affect a trade.

item.title: Move Crypto Collateral Before a Margin Call
item.description: Move collateral before liquidation by checking the venue’s threshold, transfer path, eligible assets and settlement time; repay debt or trim exposure if funds cannot arrive in time.

item.title: Compare Bridge Speed Before Moving Tokens
item.description: Bridge speed depends on source-chain confirmation, route liquidity and destination execution; compare the same transfer by usable arrival time, not the headline ETA.

item.title: How to identify wrapped tokens on a layer two
item.description: A wrapped token on a layer two is a chain-specific representation, so check its contract, origin, bridge route and redemption path before you transfer funds.

item.title: ETH to Mantle: When to Bridge and When to Use an Exchange
item.description: For ETH moving to Mantle, a bridge preserves the asset across networks, while an exchange route can trade or custody it; fees, timing and control differ.
